associations.add.description: Files › Associations › Internal Associations dialog: button adding an association. Keep it short.

associations.edit_dialog.title.description: Associate dialog (Files › Associations › Associate With, or Edit... in Internal Associations): its title. Keep it short.

associations.empty.description: Files › Associations › Internal Associations dialog: shown when there are no associations.

associations.mask_needed.description: Associate dialog (Files › Associations › Associate With, or Edit... in Internal Associations): error notification when OK is pressed with no mask. Keep *.txt as it is.

associations.remove.description: Files › Associations › Internal Associations dialog: small button of a row, removing the association. Keep it short.

associations.title.description: Files › Associations › Internal Associations dialog: its title. Keep it short.

context_menu.action_failed.description: Error notification after a desktop action of the right-click menu; name = the action's name, e.g. Compress; err = the system's reason.

context_menu.actions.description: Right-click menu on files and folders (Linux, as Dolphin's): submenu of the desktop's service menus and scripts for the files. Keep it short.

context_menu.copy.description: Right-click menu on files and folders (Linux, as Dolphin's): copies the files to the clipboard. Keep it short.

context_menu.create_new.description: Right-click menu on files and folders (Linux, as Dolphin's), on a folder: submenu making a new folder or file, its templates below. Keep it short.

context_menu.cut.description: Right-click menu on files and folders (Linux, as Dolphin's): cuts the files to the clipboard. Keep it short.

context_menu.delete.description: Right-click menu on files and folders (Linux, as Dolphin's), on a server or in an archive (no trash there): deletes the files. Keep it short.

context_menu.edit.description: Right-click menu on files and folders (Linux, as Dolphin's): opens the file in the editor, as F4. Keep it short.

context_menu.empty_file.description: Right-click menu on files and folders (Linux, as Dolphin's) › Create New: a new empty file; asks its name. Keep it short.

context_menu.move_to_trash.description: Right-click menu on files and folders (Linux, as Dolphin's), on this computer: moves the files to the trash. Use the desktop's word for the trash.

context_menu.new_file_dialog.label.description: New file dialog: the label above the name field. Keep it short.

context_menu.new_file_dialog.title.description: Title of the small dialog asking a new file's name (right-click menu › Create New). Keep it short.

context_menu.new_file_failed.description: Error notification after Create New; err = the system's reason, e.g. File exists.

context_menu.new_folder.description: Right-click menu on files and folders (Linux, as Dolphin's) › Create New: a new folder; asks its name. Keep it short.

context_menu.open.description: Right-click menu on files and folders (Linux, as Dolphin's): opens the files, as Enter does. Keep it short.

context_menu.open_failed.description: Error notification after Open With; err = the system's reason, e.g. No such file or directory.

context_menu.open_terminal_here.description: Right-click menu on files and folders (Linux, as Dolphin's), on a folder: opens the desktop's terminal in it.

context_menu.open_with.description: Right-click menu on files and folders (Linux, as Dolphin's): submenu listing the applications that open the file.

context_menu.other_application.description: Right-click menu on files and folders (Linux, as Dolphin's) › Open With: the desktop's dialog to choose another application.

context_menu.pack.description: Right-click menu on files and folders (Linux, as Dolphin's): packs the files into an archive; a dialog opens. Keep it short.

context_menu.pack_files.description: Windows: Explorer's right-click menu, an item the app adds below Copy: packs the files into an archive.

context_menu.paste.description: Right-click menu on files and folders (Linux, as Dolphin's), on a folder: pastes the files on the clipboard. Keep it short.

context_menu.properties.description: Right-click menu on files and folders (Linux, as Dolphin's): the desktop's properties dialog of the file or folder. Keep it short.

context_menu.properties_failed.description: Error notification when the desktop's properties dialog could not open; err = the system's reason.

context_menu.rename.description: Right-click menu on files and folders (Linux, as Dolphin's): renames the file; asks the new name. Keep it short.

context_menu.rename_dialog.label.description: Rename dialog: the label above the name field. Keep it short.

context_menu.rename_dialog.title.description: Title of the small dialog asking a file's new name (right-click menu › Rename). Keep it short.

context_menu.rename_failed.description: Error notification after Rename; err = the system's reason, e.g. Permission denied.

context_menu.shell_menu_failed.description: Windows: error notification when Explorer's right-click menu could not open or run; err = the system's reason.

context_menu.show_failed.description: Error notification after Show in File Manager; err = the system's reason.

context_menu.show_in_file_manager.description: Right-click menu on files and folders (Linux, as Dolphin's): opens the desktop's file manager with the files selected.

context_menu.terminal_failed.description: Error notification after Open Terminal; err = the reason, e.g. no terminal found.

context_menu.terminal_not_local.description: Warning notification: Open Terminal while the panel shows a server.
context_menu.terminal_not_local.message: A terminal opens only in this computer's folders.

context_menu.unpack.description: Right-click menu on files and folders (Linux, as Dolphin's), on archives: unpacks them; a dialog opens. Keep it short.

context_menu.view.description: Right-click menu on files (Linux and Windows): opens the file in the viewer, as F3. Keep it short.

desktop.no_app_chooser.description: The reason Open With › Other Application… failed (Linux), shown after "Could not open:"; err = the D-Bus error. Starts lowercase as it follows a colon.
desktop.no_app_chooser.message: the desktop has no app chooser ({err})

desktop.no_terminal.description: The reason no terminal opened (Linux), shown after "Could not open a terminal:"; starts lowercase as it follows a colon.

desktop.nothing_to_run.description: The reason a desktop action did not run (its command line is empty); name = the action's name, e.g. Compress.

desktop.scripts.description: Right-click menu › Actions: submenu of the user's Nautilus, Nemo or Caja scripts. Use those file managers' word. Keep it short.

file_menu.change_tags_failed.description: macOS: error notification after changing the files' tags; err = the system's reason, e.g. Permission denied.

file_menu.compress.description: macOS: right-click menu on files, as Finder's: packs the files into an archive. count = how many are chosen; with one (=1) its name is shown: name = the file's name, e.g. Report.pdf. Use Finder's wording.

file_menu.copy.description: macOS: right-click menu on files, as Finder's: copies the files to the clipboard. count = how many are chosen; with one (=1) its name is shown: name = the file's name, e.g. Report.pdf. Use Finder's wording.

file_menu.copy_path.description: macOS: right-click menu on files, as Finder's: copies the files' full paths as text.

file_menu.delete.description: macOS: right-click menu on files, as Finder's, on a server or in an archive (no Trash there): deletes the files.

file_menu.duplicate.description: macOS: right-click menu on files, as Finder's: copies each file beside itself. Use Finder's wording.

file_menu.duplicate_failed.description: macOS: error notification after Duplicate; err = the system's reason, e.g. Permission denied.

file_menu.edit_tags.description: macOS: right-click menu on files, as Finder's: opens a popover to add and remove the files' tags. Use Finder's wording.

file_menu.get_info.description: macOS: right-click menu on files, as Finder's: the file's properties. Use Finder's wording.

file_menu.make_alias.description: macOS: right-click menu on files, as Finder's: makes a Finder alias of each file. Use Finder's wording.

file_menu.make_alias_failed.description: macOS: error notification after Make Alias; err = the system's reason, e.g. Permission denied.

file_menu.move_to_trash.description: macOS: right-click menu on files, as Finder's, on this Mac: moves the files to the Trash. Use Finder's wording.

file_menu.new_folder.description: macOS: right-click menu on files, as Finder's, on a folder: makes a new folder. Use Finder's wording.

file_menu.open.description: macOS: right-click menu on files, as Finder's: opens the files. Use Finder's wording.

file_menu.open_failed.description: macOS: error notification after Open With; err = the system's reason, e.g. Permission denied.

file_menu.open_with.description: macOS: right-click menu on files, as Finder's: submenu of the applications that open the file. Use Finder's wording.

file_menu.open_with_default.description: macOS: right-click menu on files, as Finder's › Open With: the application that opens the file by default; app = its name, e.g. Preview. Use Finder's wording.

file_menu.paste.description: macOS: right-click menu on files, as Finder's, on a folder: pastes the files on the clipboard. Use Finder's wording.

file_menu.quick_look.description: macOS: right-click menu on files, as Finder's: previews the files in Quick Look (keep that name). count = how many are chosen; with one (=1) its name is shown: name = the file's name, e.g. Report.pdf. Use Finder's wording.

file_menu.quick_look_failed.description: macOS: error notification when Quick Look could not open; err = the system's reason, e.g. Permission denied.

file_menu.rename.description: macOS: right-click menu on files, as Finder's: renames the file; asks the new name. Use Finder's wording.

file_menu.reveal_failed.description: macOS: error notification after Reveal in Finder; err = the system's reason, e.g. Permission denied.
file_menu.reveal_failed.message: Could not show it in Finder: {err}

file_menu.reveal_in_finder.description: macOS: right-click menu on files, as Finder's: shows the files in a Finder window. Use Finder's wording.

file_menu.show_package_contents.description: macOS: right-click menu on files, as Finder's, on an application: opens it as a folder. Use Finder's wording.

file_menu.tag_dot.add.description: macOS: right-click menu on files, as Finder's: tooltip of a colour dot under Tags…; name = the tag's name, e.g. Red.

file_menu.tag_dot.remove.description: macOS: right-click menu on files, as Finder's: tooltip of a colour dot under Tags… that all the files have; name = the tag's name, e.g. Red.

file_menu.tags_popover.show_all.description: macOS: the Tags… popover's last row, listing the folder's other tags too. Use Finder's wording.

file_menu.tags_popover.title.description: macOS: title of the Tags… popover (Finder's). count = how many are chosen; with one (=1) its name is shown: name = the file's name, e.g. Report.pdf. Use Finder's wording. Keep it short.
file_menu.tags_popover.title.message: {count, plural, =1 {Assign tags to “{name}”} other {Assign tags to # Items}}

keys.apply.description: Configuration › Shortcuts dialog: button applying the changes, the dialog staying open. Keep it short.

keys.cancel.description: Configuration › Shortcuts dialog: button closing without the changes. Keep it short.

keys.clear.tooltip.description: Configuration › Shortcuts dialog: tooltip of the × button that removes a key. Keep it short.

keys.column.alternate.description: Configuration › Shortcuts dialog: header of the column of each command's second key. Keep it short.

keys.column.command.description: Configuration › Shortcuts dialog: header of the commands' column. Keep it short.

keys.custom.description: Configuration › Shortcuts dialog: dropdown item while the keys are none of the presets or saved sets. Keep it short.

keys.delete_set.description: Configuration › Shortcuts dialog: button deleting the chosen saved key set. Keep it short.

keys.note.custom_replaced.description: Configuration › Shortcuts dialog: note under the list after a change; after choosing a preset or set while the keys were changed; name = the preset's or set's name, e.g. Total Commander. "Save as" is the button's name.

keys.note.deleted.description: Configuration › Shortcuts dialog: note under the list after a change; after Delete; name = the set's name, e.g. My keys. OK and Apply are the buttons' names.
keys.note.deleted.message: {name} is deleted; OK or Apply makes it so.

keys.note.moved.description: Configuration › Shortcuts dialog: note under the list after a change; key = the key, e.g. Ctrl+1; command = the command it now runs, e.g. Sort by Size; other = the command that had it, e.g. Sort by Name.

keys.note.name_reserved.description: Configuration › Shortcuts dialog: note under the list after a change; after Save as with a preset's name (or Custom); name = the name typed, e.g. Krusader.
keys.note.name_reserved.message: "{name}" is a preset's name; choose another.

keys.note.press_new_key.description: Configuration › Shortcuts dialog: note under the list after a change; shown after a key's cell is clicked.
keys.note.press_new_key.message: Press the new key; Esc leaves it as it was.

keys.note.saved.description: Configuration › Shortcuts dialog: note under the list after a change; after Save as; name = the set's name, e.g. My keys. OK and Apply are the buttons' names.
keys.note.saved.message: Saved as {name}; OK or Apply keeps it.

keys.note.set.description: Configuration › Shortcuts dialog: note under the list after a change; key = the key, e.g. Ctrl+1; command = the command it now runs, e.g. Sort by Size.

keys.note.taken_by_system.description: Configuration › Shortcuts dialog: note under the list after a change; key = the key, e.g. Ctrl+F3; by = what the system does with it, e.g. KDE: switch to desktop 3.
keys.note.taken_by_system.message: {key} is taken by {by}, so it never reaches Spark Commander.

keys.ok.description: Configuration › Shortcuts dialog: button applying the changes and closing. Keep it short.

keys.press_key.description: Configuration › Shortcuts dialog: shown in a key's cell while it waits for the new key. Keep it short (the cell is narrow).

keys.reserved.text_console.description: Shortcuts dialog: what the system does with a key, so the app never gets it (shown as "Ctrl+F3 is taken by …" and in a tooltip); system = Windows, macOS, KDE, GNOME or Linux, untranslated. Ctrl+Alt+F1… switch to a text console on every Linux desktop.

keys.reserved.toolbar.description: Shortcuts dialog: what the system does with a key, so the app never gets it (shown as "Ctrl+F3 is taken by …" and in a tooltip); system = Windows, macOS, KDE, GNOME or Linux, untranslated. Moves the keyboard focus to the window's toolbar (macOS).

keys.reserved.window_menu.description: Shortcuts dialog: what the system does with a key, so the app never gets it (shown as "Ctrl+F3 is taken by …" and in a tooltip); system = Windows, macOS, KDE, GNOME or Linux, untranslated. Opens the window's own menu (move, size, close…).

keys.reserved.workspace_down.description: Shortcuts dialog: what the system does with a key, so the app never gets it (shown as "Ctrl+F3 is taken by …" and in a tooltip); system = Windows, macOS, KDE, GNOME or Linux, untranslated. Switches to the GNOME workspace below.

keys.reserved.workspace_left.description: Shortcuts dialog: what the system does with a key, so the app never gets it (shown as "Ctrl+F3 is taken by …" and in a tooltip); system = Windows, macOS, KDE, GNOME or Linux, untranslated. Switches to the GNOME workspace on the left.

keys.reserved.workspace_right.description: Shortcuts dialog: what the system does with a key, so the app never gets it (shown as "Ctrl+F3 is taken by …" and in a tooltip); system = Windows, macOS, KDE, GNOME or Linux, untranslated. Switches to the GNOME workspace on the right.

keys.reserved.workspace_up.description: Shortcuts dialog: what the system does with a key, so the app never gets it (shown as "Ctrl+F3 is taken by …" and in a tooltip); system = Windows, macOS, KDE, GNOME or Linux, untranslated. Switches to the GNOME workspace above.

keys.reset.tooltip.description: Configuration › Shortcuts dialog: tooltip of a row's undo button; preset = the preset's name, e.g. Total Commander.

keys.reset_all.description: Configuration › Shortcuts dialog: button undoing all the changes to the keys. Keep it short.

keys.save_as.button.description: Configuration › Shortcuts dialog: button saving the keys as they are under a name. Keep it short.

keys.save_as.default_name.description: Save shortcuts dialog: the name it offers first for the user's own key set.

keys.save_as.label.description: Save shortcuts dialog: the label above the name field. Keep it short.

keys.save_as.title.description: Title of the small dialog asking the name to save the keys under (Shortcuts › Save as…). Keep it short.

keys.search.placeholder.description: Configuration › Shortcuts dialog: placeholder of the search field above the list.
keys.search.placeholder.message: Search for a command or a key

keys.set_label.description: Configuration › Shortcuts dialog: label before the dropdown of key sets (the presets Spark Commander, Total Commander…, the user's own sets). Keep it short.

keys.taken_by.tooltip.description: Configuration › Shortcuts dialog: tooltip of the warning sign on a key the system takes; by = what the system does with it, e.g. KDE: switch to desktop 3.

keys.title.description: Configuration › Shortcuts dialog: its title. Keep it short.

mark.compare.marked.description: Notification after Mark › Compare Directories › Mark Newer; count = how many files it marked on both sides, e.g. 12.
mark.compare.marked.message: {count, plural, one {# file marked: newer than, or missing on, the other side.} other {# files marked: newer than, or missing on, the other side.}}

mark.compare.same.description: Notification after Mark › Compare Directories › Mark Newer when nothing differs.
mark.compare.same.message: The folders have the same files.

mark.load_selection.label.description: Load selection dialog: the label above the file's path.
mark.load_selection.label.message: Select the names listed in the file:

mark.load_selection.title.description: Title of the dialog of Mark › Selection › Load Selection From File. Keep it short.

mark.save_selection.label.description: Save selection dialog: the label above the file's path.
mark.save_selection.label.message: Save the selected names to the file:

mark.save_selection.title.description: Title of the dialog of Mark › Selection › Save Selection To File. Keep it short.

mark.select_group.label.description: Select group dialog: the label above the mask field. Keep the masks as they are.
mark.select_group.label.message: Select the files (*.txt *.md; a folder mask ends in /):

mark.select_group.title.description: Title of the dialog of Mark › Select Group (Num +), which marks the files matching a mask. Keep it short.

mark.selection_file.not_local.description: Warning notification: Mark › Selection › Save or Load Selection (to or from a file) while the panel shows a server or an archive.
mark.selection_file.not_local.message: Selection files are kept on this computer, outside archives.

mark.unselect_group.label.description: Unselect group dialog: the label above the mask field. Keep the masks as they are.
mark.unselect_group.label.message: Unselect the files (*.txt *.md; a folder mask ends in /):

mark.unselect_group.title.description: Title of the dialog of Mark › Unselect Group (Num -), which unmarks the files matching a mask. Keep it short.

menus.hide_app.description: macOS: the application menu (the one named Spark Commander) in the menu bar. Hides the app's windows; use macOS's own wording.

menus.hide_others.description: macOS: the application menu (the one named Spark Commander) in the menu bar. Hides the other apps; use macOS's own wording.

menus.minimize.description: macOS: an item of the Window menu in the menu bar; use macOS's own word.

menus.quit_app.description: macOS: the application menu (the one named Spark Commander) in the menu bar. Use macOS's own wording.

menus.services.description: macOS: the application menu (the one named Spark Commander) in the menu bar. The system's Services submenu; use macOS's own word.

menus.show_all.description: macOS: the application menu (the one named Spark Commander) in the menu bar. Shows the hidden apps again; use macOS's own wording.

menus.zoom.description: macOS: an item of the Window menu in the menu bar; use macOS's own word. Makes the window as large as it needs.

shells.command_prompt.description: Windows: Settings › Terminal, the shell list: Windows' cmd.exe. Use Windows' own name for it in the language.

tools.clear_key.description: Tools › Manage Tools dialog: button removing the tool's key. Keep it short.

tools.close.description: Tools › Manage Tools dialog: button closing the dialog. Keep it short.

tools.delete.description: Tools › Manage Tools dialog: button deleting the selected tool. Keep it short.

tools.empty.description: Tools › Manage Tools dialog: shown in the empty list. "New..." is the button's name.
tools.empty.message: No tools yet: New... adds one.

tools.field.command.description: Tools › Manage Tools dialog: label of the tool's command line field. Keep it short (80 px).

tools.field.key.description: Tools › Manage Tools dialog: label of the tool's key. Keep it short (80 px).

tools.field.name.description: Tools › Manage Tools dialog: label of the tool's name field. Keep it short (80 px).

tools.intro.description: Tools › Manage Tools dialog: the line on top. Tools is the menu's name.
tools.intro.message: Your own command lines, in the Tools menu: click one there, or press its key.

tools.key.none.description: Tools › Manage Tools dialog: shown as the tool's key when it has none. Keep it short.

tools.key.waiting.description: Tools › Manage Tools dialog: shown as the tool's key while it waits for one. Esc is the key's name.

tools.move_down.description: Tools › Manage Tools dialog: tooltip of the ↓ button moving the tool down the list.

tools.move_up.description: Tools › Manage Tools dialog: tooltip of the ↑ button moving the tool up the list.

tools.name.placeholder.description: Tools › Manage Tools dialog: example shown in the empty name field (a tool comparing the file with the other panel's).

tools.new.description: Tools › Manage Tools dialog: button adding a tool. Keep it short.

tools.new_name.description: Tools › Manage Tools dialog: the name a new tool gets; number = the first free number, e.g. 2.

tools.no_command.description: Warning notification when a tool without a command line is run; tool = its name, e.g. Tool 1. "Tools > Manage Tools" are the menu's and its item's names: use their translations.
tools.no_command.message: {tool} has no command yet: Tools > Manage Tools.

tools.not_local.description: Warning notification when a tool is run while the panel shows a server or an archive.
tools.not_local.message: Tools run on this computer: the panel shows a server or an archive.

tools.note.key_of_command.description: Tools › Manage Tools dialog: warning after setting a key a command has; key = the key, e.g. Ctrl+M; command = the command's name, e.g. Multi-Rename Tool.
tools.note.key_of_command.message: {key} is also {command}: the tool takes it.

tools.note.key_of_other_tool.description: Tools › Manage Tools dialog: warning after setting a key another tool has; key = the key, e.g. Ctrl+Shift+M; tool = the other tool's name, e.g. Meld.
tools.note.key_of_other_tool.message: {key} is {tool}'s too: the lower one in the list takes it.

tools.placeholders.description: Tools › Manage Tools dialog: small print explaining the codes a command line may have. Keep every %-code (%P, %T, %N, %O, %E, %S, %%) and "%P%N" exactly as they are.
tools.placeholders.message: %P this panel's folder, %T the other panel's (both end in a separator, so "%P%N" is a path), %N the file under the cursor, %O its name without the extension, %E the extension, %S the selected files (else the cursor's), each quoted; %% a %. Put quotes around the rest: "%P%N".

tools.run_in_terminal.description: Tools › Manage Tools dialog: check box: the tool runs in the built-in terminal.
tools.run_in_terminal.message: Run in the terminal, to see what it prints

tools.set_key.description: Tools › Manage Tools dialog: button: the next key pressed becomes the tool's. Keep it short.

tools.title.description: Tools › Manage Tools dialog: its title. Keep it short.
